correctness.rationale: Conditionally on each realized length vector, pairwise spherical inner products are orthogonal with variance \(1/d\), giving exact normalized variance one. A Gaussian-polar coupling reduces the angular statistic to \(d\) iid unit-variance Gaussian quadratic forms, each with fourth moment at most \(15\). The angular-radial coupling error is exactly \(2\operatorname{Var}(\|G\|/\sqrt d)\le2/d\). A Wasserstein Stein bound proves \(W_1\le(3\cdot15^{3/4}+\sqrt 2)/\sqrt d<25/\sqrt d\). All boundaries and computations are specified in RESULT.md; finite checks supplement the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The strong feature is uniformity over arbitrary growth of the number of steps and every realized dependent-length vector, with no length moments. This replaces the motivating paper's first-order angular-error estimates by a conditional second-order distributional approximation, making it useful even when unnormalized errors fail to converge. The Gaussian radial comparison is a reusable structural proof of that unusual uniformity, not an arbitrary numerical constant or relabeling.
